title: Better scores, but more learning?
lines: The classroom's activity scores rise, but can students solve a new problem without the platform?
The Art of Knowing What Matters argues that schools and AI should be judged by the abilities they help people develop.
A fast answer can hide uncertainty, while slower work may contain the learning a metric misses.

title: An answer becomes a capacity
lines: The book asks how information becomes something we can use, and how we decide what matters.
It follows education, institutions, and AI to examine which abilities our systems help people develop.
What gets lost when a complicated situation becomes a convenient summary or score?

emotionalPlan.purpose: Distinguish visible performance from learning and practical judgment in educational and institutional systems.
emotionalPlan.visualActing: Separate answer, explanation and judgment using one learning task.
voiceDirections: Plain curiosity; gently emphasize “what matters”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
Grounded interest; gently emphasize “help people develop”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
Quiet doubt; gently emphasize “summary or score”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

title: The judgment behind progress
lines: Teachers, builders, and curious readers can use these examples to question what counts as progress.
Begin in the classroom, where an excellent report may still be asking the wrong question.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Distinguish visible performance from learning and practical judgment in educational and institutional systems.
